blogs.content: Blog How one DTC brand built 100+ CX automations with no IT-dependency { const isEventSignup = false; if (isEventSignup && window.dataLayer) { window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'event_cta_click', cta_location: 'hero', event_slug: 'blog-cx-automation-without-engineers', page_path: window.location.pathname }); } const matched = isEventSignup && typeof plab !== 'undefined' && plab.scrollToEventForm ? plab.scrollToEventForm() : null; if (matched === null && typeof plab !== 'undefined' && plab.scroll) { plab.scroll(document.querySelector('.Resource__Body'), -80); } })()" class="wp-block-button__link wp-element-button has-text-xs-font-size !py-3 !px-4"> Keep reading Back to Resource Hub published on July 22, 2026 = 1080 ? open = true : open = false;" @resize.window="window.outerWidth >= 1080 ? open = true : open = false;" class="w-full lg:w-[36%]"> Contents From six manual follow-ups to 100+ automations: How one CX leader built an automation engine without an IT team Scaling the human touch – from six manual touches to two or three Cutting contact rate from 26% to 15% – in three iterations Eliminating the hidden cost of context switching The pattern: what all three automations have in common Start with the follow-up From six manual follow-ups to 100+ automations: How one CX leader built an automation engine without an IT team “We’d love to automate – but we don’t have the engineering team for it.” If you’ve said this, or heard it in a meeting, or quietly thought it while watching another brand’s case study, here’s the update: this excuse died in 2026. CX automation without engineers is no longer a contradiction — the tools for building it are more accessible than ever. Taylor Johnson is the Director of Customer Experience at Nathan James , a fully online DTC furniture brand selling flat-pack furniture through their own site, Amazon, Wayfair and other major retailers. Her team: 21 frontline agents, two team leads. No software engineers, no automation specialists. Her automation count: over 100. IT involvement: one automation. The rest she built with her team. “There’s just no excuse nowadays. I think it’s so important for people to not be afraid to step out of the comfort zone and explore those more technical areas that they’ve not explored before. Building code, building JavaScript, anything like that is possible now with the tools that we have.” What follows are three real automations Taylor built. Each one follows the same pattern: Identify a low-risk, high-impact process Choose the simplest tool that works Iterate and measure. None required a software team or a transformation budget – but all produced measurable results. Scaling the human touch – from six manual touches to two or three The problem: Nathan James had a signature move. When a customer reported a product issue and the team sent a replacement, an agent would manually follow up once the replacement was delivered. A simple message: “Hey, saw this got delivered, just want to check in and make sure everything’s good now.” Customers loved it, as feedback showed. In times where post-purchase acts as a hidden growth-engine , the follow-up was a genuine brand signal – the kind of touch that separates “fine” customer service from “I’m telling my friends about this.” At the same time it was crushing agent capacity. Every replacement ticket required the agent to: monitor delivery status, notice when it arrived, manually craft the follow-up, wait for the customer’s response and close the loop. From open to close, the average ticket required at least six touches. The solution: A native Shopify integration with their help desk. The workflow listens for “order delivered” events in Shopify, then layers two conditions: Is this a replacement order? Does it have an open conversation? If both conditions are met, the system automatically sends the check-in message. No AI, no third-party automation platform, no code. Just a deterministic workflow using tools the team already had access to. The critical design choice: instead of using a template or an AI-generated version, the automated message was copied directly from what agents were already saying. The result: Average touches per ticket dropped from six to two or three. Customers can’t tell the difference. The high-touch feel survived intact – because the message is the human message, just delivered automatically. The lesson: This automation was free. It used native integrations between two tools the team already paid for. If your help desk connects to your eCommerce platform, you can probably build something like this today. Start with the message your agents already send, automate the delivery – and that’s it. Cutting contact rate from 26% to 15% – in three iterations The problem: Nathan James introduced backorder and preorder functionality – letting customers buy products before they were physically in the warehouse. The only customer-facing information was a single line on the product page: “Estimated to ship on [date].” Contact rate exploded to 25–26% (conversations divided by related orders). Customers couldn’t remember their ship date, wanted to check if it had changed, or hadn’t noticed it in the first place. WISMO – “where is my order?” – on steroids. “Ideally in a perfect world, we would have had some of those automations in place before then. Obviously it’s not an ideal world. So sometimes you just got to roll with the punches.” Taylor’s first lesson from this experience: build the automation infrastructure before you launch the customer-facing feature – not after the contact rate spike forces you to. Iteration one: Email updates. The team funneled all backorder and preorder data into an Airtable table, connected Airtable to Klaviyo and sent customers email updates with their estimated ship date. Date changes triggered immediate notifications. Better – but not solved. Emails got lost in spam and promotions folders. Customers didn’t always see them. And because estimated ship dates could change daily or weekly, frequent emails risked inbox fatigue. The team had to balance “keep me informed” with “stop emailing me.” Iteration two: The insight. Customers were already visiting their order status page repeatedly. They expected to see the estimated ship date there, but the page showed nothing. The answer wasn’t more emails. It was meeting customers where they already were. Iteration three: Shopify metafields on the order status page. Taylor’s team created a Shopify metafield to attach the estimated ship date as custom data to each order. An automation synced the date from Airtable to the Shopify order metafield, refreshed daily. If the date changed in Airtable, it updated on the order status page automatically. The software team added a small piece of code to the Shopify theme to render the metafield on the order status page. This was the only IT-assisted piece across all three automations. The message to customers became simple: “Check your order status page anytime – it always shows the latest estimated ship date.” The tooling twist: Taylor’s default automation tool is Make. But Make charges per item processed. With 2,000 to 3,000 orders to sync daily, the credit math broke down fast. She switched this specific workflow to n8n, which charges per workflow execution rather than per item. Same 3,000 orders, one execution. Significant cost savings. The result: Contact rate dropped from 26% to 15–16% – with a significant portion of that reduction driven by these automation improvements. In absolute terms: roughly 800 to 1,000 fewer contacts per month. Approximately 60 to 70 hours of team time saved monthly. The lesson: Iterate. The first version doesn’t have to be the final one. blogs.title: 6 Labor Day Marketing Ideas to Set Your Brand Up for a Strong Q4
blogs.author: Emily Riedy
blogs.content: Turn Labor Day into Q4 momentum Generated by Klaviyo AI The article explains how to use Labor Day campaigns to clear inventory, grow messaging lists, and collect actionable customer data. It outlines six tactics that connect Labor Day promotions to stronger personalization, higher revenue, and better retention heading into Q4. Leverage deal-driven segments Use Labor Day free gift and clearance offers to identify discount-motivated shoppers, segment them, and target them with future flash sales and steep discounts. Grow mobile messaging Treat Labor Day as a list-building moment for SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, using early-access and clearance incentives to create high-intent subscribers for the rest of the year. Reward and segment VIPs Segment top customers by behavior and loyalty tier, then offer tailored perks like early access, personalized recommendations, and bonus points to deepen relationships. Activate social proof and data Collect detailed reviews, UGC, and browsing signals, then use them—along with wishlists and recently viewed items—to power personalized recommendations and AI search visibility. Scale support with AI Deploy AI customer agents and self-serve hubs to answer questions, recommend products, apply promotions, and convert Labor Day browsers into buyers at scale. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary Between the barbecues and the beach trips, Labor Day shoppers still find time to spend. According to Klaviyo's 2025 Labor Day weekend sales data , US ecommerce sales were up 8% across the long weekend in 2025 compared to 2024, and up 10% on Labor Day itself. Labor Day lands between back-to-school and Q4 holiday shopping events, making it a natural bridge between two big spending moments. It’s an opportunity to build your text message list, reward your best customers, gather reviews, and learn which customers respond to which offers. This is all useful preparation for Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM), when it’s time to put all the customer data you’ve gathered throughout the year to work. According to Klaviyo’s 2025 Future of Consumer Marketing Report , 74% of consumers now expect personalized experiences from brands. Labor Day is a great opportunity to gather the zero- and first-party customer data that makes personalization possible year-round. Here are 6 Labor Day marketing ideas to help you make the most of the holiday and build customer relationships that last well beyond it. Align your marketing campaigns with relevant holidays and year-round celebrations. Get your marketing campaign calendar 1. Pair Labor Day seasonal clearance with free gifts A Labor Day free gift offer is a good way to move summer inventory and make way for fall products. But it’s even better for learning who your discount-driven customers are. What can look like a one-and-done sale is actually a source of customer data you can use to drive more revenue throughout the year. Customers who take advantage of a free gift are a distinct audience segment : they’re deal-driven, and they’re motivated by different incentives than your high spenders or brand loyalists. If you end up running this offer, make sure to create a segment for the people who buy from it. You’ll want to target them with future clearance offers, flash sales, and steep discounts. Over time, these customers may spend more if they like your products. In the meantime, honor the way they spend now and target them with bigger discounts when you can offer them. Labor Day marketing idea: Laura Geller offers tiered free gifts alongside sitewide discounts In this Labor Day marketing example, beauty brand Laura Geller runs a tiered free gift offer alongside a sitewide discount, giving customers a reason to increase their order value. Shoppers who spend $55 worth of products get a free mini primer, and those who spend $75 get a full-size mascara on top of that. The tiered structure serves two purposes: it moves inventory, and it surfaces which customers respond to a good deal within certain product categories. This is spending and product preference data you can act on long after Labor Day is over. Subject line: Geller Gal, Your Labor Day Steals Are Here 🚨 Source: Milled 2. Build your mobile messaging programs with Labor Day sale incentives SMS marketing revenue jumped 48% YoY during Labor Day 2025, and roughly one-third of that revenue came from first-time buyers, according to Klaviyo's 2025 Labor Day weekend sales data. Even with higher send volumes, revenue per send held strong, which means consumers are receptive to timely texts. 2024 research from Klaviyo and Recharge also supports the idea that people who opt in to receive texts from your brand really want to hear from you: the survey found that 72% of people are willing to receive a text at least once a week. All of that means the size of your text message marketing list going into Labor Day weekend has a direct impact on revenue for the rest of the year. Whether you’re promoting a summer clearance sale, an end-of-season discount, or early access to deals, Labor Day is a natural hook for text message sign-ups—and once someone’s on your list, you can reach them all year-round. SMS has been a go-to channel for Labor Day campaigns for years, but RCS marketing and WhatsApp are also worth adding to your mobile messaging mix. Here’s what that might look like: RCS turns traditional texts into interactive shopping experiences with carousels, images, and tappable buttons. For a Labor Day summer clearance sale, you could showcase end-of-season products in a swipeable carousel, complete with discounted prices and one-tap purchase links. A WhatsApp Labor Day campaign could start with a clearance sale image and a quick reply prompt: “Want early access?” Customers who tap yes get an automated follow-up with personalized product recommendations based on their past purchases. Rather than a one-way promotional message, the exchange captures customer preferences and guides each shopper to the most relevant products. Labor Day marketing idea: Use Labor Day to grow your text messaging subscriber list Two weeks before Labor Day, add a pop-up to your site with a simple offer targeted at existing email subscribers: sign up for texts or WhatsApp, and get early access to the Labor Day sale before it goes public. Around a week before Labor Day weekend, send the early-access text. Follow up on Saturday with a reminder highlighting your bestsellers, and again on Sunday with a last-chance message calling out anything that's running low on stock. By Tuesday, you’ve hopefully made headway on clearing out your summer inventory. You’ve also created a list of high-intent subscribers who are warmed up to hear from you for BFCM. 3. Reserve something special for your VIPs on Labor Day Your VIPs already know your brand and have shown you they'll keep coming back. They've earned something more than a sitewide discount code, and Labor Day is a good moment to reward them. But it’s also important to remember that not all VIPs are the same. Ahead of Labor Day, segment your most valuable customers by purchase frequency, spend threshold, and loyalty tier to build an offer that fits each group. Here are a few ways to target these VIP segments during Labor Day: Send frequent buyers an early-access code they can use 24 hours before the general sale goes live. Send high spenders personalized product recommendations, with a free gift on orders above their typical spend threshold. Give top loyalty tier members bonus points for every Labor Day purchase, moving them closer to their next reward. Labor Day marketing idea: Caitlyn Minimalist turns Labor Day into a VIP event In this Labor Day marketing example, jewelry brand Caitlyn Minimalist invites subscribers to a Labor Day TikTok LIVE event featuring VIP gift boxes, flash sales, and grand prizes. The email leads with exclusivity, urgency, and a clear breakdown of what to expect: free jewelry, limited-time deals only available during the event, and ...

blogs.title: Klaviyo New Integrations: Figma, Yotpo, & Two More Worth Knowing
blogs.author: Joan Morales
blogs.content: AI overview Generated by Klaviyo AI Klaviyo announced four new integrations to help B2C marketers act on customer data in real time: Figma for one-click asset exports, Yotpo for loyalty-triggered email/SMS flows, Contentsquare for behavioral cohort targeting, and Fairing for automated survey response follow-ups. These integrations eliminate manual data transfers by feeding live signals directly into marketing automation, enabling timely, personalized customer communications based on design assets, loyalty status, site behavior, and direct feedback. Sign up Get a demo Show AI generated summary A customer earns loyalty points, then gets the same generic email as everyone else. Another stalls at check-out and never hears from you again. A third fills out a post-purchase survey and tells you exactly how they feel, and the next message they get ignores every word of it. Those missed opportunities aren’t happening because you don’t have enough data. They’re happening because there’s a gap between where your customer signals live and where your marketing actually runs. 4 new Q2 integrations in Klaviyo, the autonomous B2C CRM, close that gap across the customer lifecycle. Figma: Get branded assets into Klaviyo in one click Export any frame, graphic, or component straight from Figma into your Klaviyo image library , with no downloading, renaming, or re-uploading files by hand. Figma is where your brand visuals get made, and now it connects directly to your image library in Klaviyo. The creative your designers finalize is ready to drop into an automated flow the same day, not 3 email threads later. Batch-export a set of assets in one job, and connect more than one Klaviyo account to switch between brands without exporting to the wrong one. For teams running multiple brands, that means building creative once from a single design source instead of rebuilding it in every account. Picture the handoff: a designer finalizes a campaign banner, exports it in one click, and it's in a flow template that same afternoon. No file swap, no version confusion. Yotpo Loyalty: Make loyalty data trigger email and SMS flows Yotpo Loyalty syncs points, tiers, rewards, and referral activity into your Klaviyo segments , flows, Customer Hub, and campaigns, so all of them react the moment a loyalty event happens. Instead of loyalty living in its own silo, it becomes a marketing trigger. Start automated flows based on loyalty events like points earned, tier changes, and reward expiration reminders. Build precise segments using more than 25 loyalty customer properties to send more relevant campaigns to the people who actually care about them. Referral activity synced from Yotpo Loyalty can also trigger an automated follow-up when a customer refers a friend or when that referral converts, so the thank-you message and the next offer arrive right on time. Let’s say a customer's reward is about to expire, and they get a text message nudge to use it. If they don't open it within a day, a follow-up email lands in their inbox with the same offer. When your repeat buyers feel seen and special, they’re more likely to keep coming back, spend more, and bring their friends with them. Contentsquare: Use behavioral data to trigger smarter campaigns Sync behavioral cohorts from Contentsquare into Klaviyo, and what happens on your site directly shapes what customers receive next. Contentsquare connects your digital experience analytics to your marketing automation. Automatically sync behavioral cohorts to trigger win-back flows for people who stall in the funnel, or target your most active visitors based on high-frequency site activity. With the Contentsquare x Klaviyo integration, cohorts update automatically as customer behavior shifts, so your segments stay current without manual list edits. You don't rebuild a list every week. The data does it for you. It works both directions. Send Klaviyo marketing data back to Contentsquare to see how your owned channels drive long-term behavior and lifetime value, not just the next click. Fairing: Put post-purchase survey responses to work automatically Fairing syncs every post-purchase survey response to Klaviyo in real time as events and custom profile properties, ready to power your flows and segments the moment a customer responds. This is zero-party data at work: information customers volunteer directly, in their own words. Use attribution data to understand which channels drive your highest-value customers, deliver Net Promoter Score (NPS) surveys directly through Klaviyo email and text messaging , and trigger personalized follow-up sequences based on exactly what customers tell you. Here’s how this might work in practice: a low NPS score drops the customer into an apology and support flow that offers the customer various methods to resolve the issue. A high score triggers a review or referral request while enthusiasm is fresh. Same survey, two automatic follow-ups. Connect all 4 integrations through the Klaviyo App Marketplace With these new integrations, customer signals flow into Klaviyo from design, loyalty, site behavior, and surveys. Your creative, campaign segments, and flows react accordingly. Each of these partners connects through the Klaviyo App Marketplace. Explore integrations Joan Morales Joan Morales is an accomplished technology executive with more than 20 years of leadership experience in partner marketing, strategic alliances, business development, and demand generation. He has successfully built and scaled global partner marketing organizations at Klaviyo, Zoom, Nutanix, and Axcient, consistently delivering strategic growth and high-impact programs across the Cloud, SaaS, Enterprise Software, and Hardware industries. Originally from Barcelona and now based in the San Francisco Bay Area, Joan is passionate about developing robust partner ecosystems and driving innovation through scalable, AI-powered partner marketing initiatives. He frequently speaks on topics related to AI in channel marketing and effective partner ecosystem strategies. Joan holds executive education credentials from the Haas School of Business at UC Berkeley, ESADE Business School, and Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona).
